rows.form_notes: projection renders all events in the "Failed password" format, collapsing the observed 48 pam_unix "other" rows into the same shape
rows.rationale: The measurement records delta_kind present, keyed on user.name = "root" (seq 1: two rows, 172.18.0.6/root, 48 "other" + 48 "password" = 96) versus every live control showing user.name "svc.reports" (C-14d/C-21d 42+42); user.name is not an unstable identifier, so this is the real distinction. The projection emits root sshd Failed-password failures on web-2 across 19:52–19:55, exactly the distinguishing field the delta turns on, and correctly placeholders the source IP (<office-ws-1-ip>) and port (<src-port>) — both unstated by the story and, for source.ip, an unstable-identifier column that matches C-21d anyway. No concrete value is fabricated: host web-2, sshd, failure outcome, and root are all story-grounded. The only divergence is granularity — the projection expresses the whole burst in the "Failed password for root" format rather than splitting the pam_unix "other" half — which is a shape difference, not a missed or invented delta.
rows.evidence: Query seq 1 returns two rows in the observed window — source.ip 172.18.0.6, user.name "root", auth_method "other" (48 failures, 19:52:23→19:55:21) and auth_method "password" (48 failures, 19:52:25→19:55:23), totalling 96 — while all live controls return user.name "svc.reports" (C-14d and C-21d: 42 + 42 failures each; C-28d empty). The distinguishing field is user.name (root vs svc.reports), which is not in the unstable-identifier list; source.ip 172.18.0.6 matches C-21d anyway and would not on its own count. Seq 2 corroborates in a surfaced field: observed failures spread across four minute-buckets (23/28/33/12, 19:52–19:55) with sample_msg "Failed password for root from 172.18.0.6 …", versus baseline bursts compressed into one or two buckets (84 in a single minute at C-14d; 77+7 at C-21d) with sample_msg naming svc.reports. Seq 3/4 (the 24h pre-window counts, 48 and 16) are lower than their live controls (672/1008/864 and 336/504/432) but non-zero, so nothing reads as suppressed, and no query contradicts the present verdict; the truncated seq 0 payload (5 of 96 hits) is consistent and was not needed to decide.

Accepted queries (seq 0/seq 2) legitimately show no delta, but the lead as a whole
carries the failure delta, and the projection omits it entirely.
